name: VECTOR UNIFIED
tagline: One 64-dimensional space holding 20,719 basketball, football and soccer careers — and a gate log that keeps score of how much of it is actually earned.
dims: 64-d joint embedding. Per-sport encoders (hoops 64-d, gridiron 32-d, pitch 24-d) feed a shared trunk (adapter + era), L2-normalised to 64-d; 3 PCA axes are exported for display only, interpretation deferred.

headline_stats.label: How much sport identity survives the joint space — model 0.6851 against a 0.6258 majority-class floor
Cross-sport nearest neighbour shares the archetype (random baseline 0.1712)
Top-10 retrieval hit rate on the 40 hand-curated named pairs
Declared archetypes that no row is ever assigned

insights.title: The sport-invariance gate is a ceiling, and the bar it used to carry sat below the floor
insights.body: G2 asks a classifier to name a row's sport from its joint vector, and it passes when accuracy comes in AT OR UNDER the target — lower is better, because a genuinely shared space should make the league unguessable. The classes are hoops 12,966 / gridiron 5,323 / pitch 2,430, so always answering 'hoops' scores 0.6258, and a perfectly sport-invariant embedding hands the classifier nothing but that same class prior. 0.6258 is the floor. A globally shuffled z scores 0.6257, which confirms it empirically. The retired target of 0.4333 came from '1/3 + 0.10' on the assumption of balanced classes, so it sat below the floor and was unreachable: a flawless invariant embedding would have failed it, and so does the trivial majority-class predictor. The current target 0.7258 is majority + 0.10, the model scores 0.6851, and the status reads 'met'. That replaced an impossible bar with an achievable one — but 'met' is weak and the file says so itself: it means within ten points of a floor anyone hits by guessing. The number to read is the gap over the floor, 0.0593. Sport identity is still partly recoverable from the joint vector.
insights.source: assets/unified.json → g2_sport_acc / g2_target / g2_majority_baseline / g2_delta_vs_majority / g2_status / g2_note; data/gate_nonvacuity.json → g2_baseline_correction, g2_null_lands_at_floor

insights.title: A gate that read 0.0 for months, because a mask was used as an index
insights.body: G1 checks that folding a sport into the joint space does not cost it its own native structure. Its position arm reported pos_drop = 0.0 for all three sports from Phase 2 until 2026-08-03 and meant nothing: knn5_acc indexed with the int64 position mask instead of masking with it, so both arms scored exactly 1.0 — on the real embedding and a shuffled one alike — and the difference was 0.0 by construction. The verdict is read straight out of the checkpoint, so re-exporting reproduces the bad value forever; only a retrain moves it. The shipped asset therefore substitutes measured values from the fixed probe. Convention is baseline minus joint, so negative means the joint space is better: hoops −0.0526 (0.7385 → 0.7911), gridiron 0.0000 (0.9991, already at ceiling), pitch +0.0021 (0.8930 → 0.8909). The gate still passes, and now it passes on evidence — a globally shuffled z degrades the same measure by +0.5493 / +0.6920 / +0.5617.
insights.source: assets/unified.json → g1_verdict, g1_pos_source, g1_pos_caveat; data/unified_report.json → G1_per_sport_noninferiority

insights.title: Half the archetype taxonomy is declared and never used
insights.body: Twelve archetypes A0–A11 are hand-authored, but only six ever get assigned: A2 (5,159 rows), A1 (4,860), A3 (3,983), A11 (3,058), A0 (2,348), A5 (1,311). A4 (defensive disruptor) is deferred with a measured reason — its only native-cluster members were pitch-side (cluster 2, 81% DEF) with no hoops or gridiron counterpart, so cross-sport analogy was trivially impossible and G4 hit 0.000; that cluster now folds into A3. A6/A7 (pedigree), A8/A9 (career arc) and A10 (elite two-way) have no native-cluster members in any sport, and the feature-based labeller for them is deferred. The gaps are structural, not incidental: the gridiron feed is offense-only skill positions because the open data has no defensive players, and pitch carries no pedigree or career data at all.
insights.source: data/archetype_map.json → archetypes_deferred_v0, archetypes_in_scope_v0, scope_note_v0; assets/unified.json → players[].cross_arch counts

insights.title: The famous-pair analogies do not retrieve, and the salvage metric was withdrawn
insights.body: Forty hand-curated cross-sport pairs (Tom Brady / Stephen Curry, Patrick Mahomes / Kevin De Bruyne, and so on) were scored by asking whether the intended partner shows up near the query. None landed in the top 10. The mean rank of the intended partner is 2114.18 against a random expectation of 2067.15, giving a better-than-random ratio of 0.978 where 1.0 is chance and higher is better — indistinguishable from random, marginally on the wrong side of it. An earlier 3.287 figure came from assuming a random rank of N/2, which is wrong because the score takes the minimum rank over all of the partner's rows; both a closed form and a 200-draw simulation now back the corrected baseline. What survives is the coarser claim: archetype agreement on the curated pairs is 0.65 against a computed random baseline of 0.1621, and the automated all-players G4 is 0.9828 against 0.1712. The space groups roles; it does not retrieve individuals.
insights.source: data/analogy_triples_report.json → retrieval_top10_hit_rate_informational, mean_b_rank, random_expected_rank, better_than_random_ratio, metric_note, G4_curated_arch_agreement, arch_agreement_random_baseline

insights.title: Tennis was probed for a fourth sport and deliberately left out
insights.body: 4,022 tennis rows were clustered at k=6 with the quality axis explicitly projected out first. PC1 still took 0.3748 of the variance and loaded on WIN_RATE 0.41, DRAW_PROGRESS_MEAN 0.402 and GAMES_WON_PCT 0.397 — the partition separates players by how good they are, not by what they do. The verdict is QUALITY TIERING, and the file records that naming these clusters would repeat the role-versus-trajectory category error, so it proposes no names at all. One cluster survived a per-cluster test for being role-like rather than tiered: cluster 4, n=487, flat on quality and extreme on SURFACE_SPECIALISATION at z=1.655.
insights.source: data/tennis_archetype_probe.json → verdict, pc1_variance_share, pc1_top_loadings, role_like_clusters, per_cluster.4, naming_note

caveat: Every number here is read from the listed files; the shipped model is UnifiedTrunk Stage 2.1 (unfrozen encoders, best_epoch=58) built 2026-07-30. Four things to hold onto. (1) G2's companion metric, effective rank (12.0), is not testable by the null suite — a row permutation leaves the spectrum untouched, so both shuffles score exactly the real value, and random Gaussian rows score HIGHER at 64.0. It detects collapse and nothing more. (2) G3's archetype separation of 0.9385 is real against a permutation null whose 95th percentile is 0.0374, but the within- and between-archetype samples draw different sport-pair mixes, with a composition gap up to 8.9 percentage points — part of that separation may be a sport-pair effect rather than an archetype effect, and the file measures the imbalance without claiming how much. (3) data/analogy_triples_report.json's metric_note still quotes the old Stage 1 G4 figure of 0.9401 inside its prose; the shipped Stage 2.1 value in data/analogy_report.json is 0.9828, and that is the one used above. (4) The game's VOR deltas are in each sport's own replacement-value units, which are not on a common scale — hoops deltas run much wider than gridiron ones, so a round is a comparison of two separately-scaled numbers, not a claim that a basketball season is worth more than a football one.

game.axis_label: VOR delta — second-half mean minus first-half mean, in each sport's own units
game.explainer: The DIRECTION axis splits a career in half and subtracts: mean value-over-replacement across the second half minus the first half. Positive means the player got better, negative means they faded. It is deliberately independent of draft standing — a player can have beaten his draft slot and still be declining. 566 hoops careers and 432 gridiron careers were scored, requiring at least 4 seasons; the top and bottom 20% get the D0 (rising) and D1 (declining) labels. Careers spent entirely below replacement are dropped rather than labelled, since VOR floors at zero and 'bad then bad' is not a direction. Hoops and gridiron VOR are on separate scales, so compare the arcs, not the raw magnitudes.

harden: 12.04 up to 19.92 across 17 seasons, delta +7.88, D0. allen: 3.01 up to 6.17 across 8 seasons, delta +3.17, D0. Both rising; the model reads harden's climb as the larger one in his own sport's units.

westbrook: 20.46 down to 13.25 across 18 seasons, delta -7.22, D1. adams: 3.93 up to 7.43 across 12 seasons, delta +3.49, D0.
Both fell. nowitzki: 14.33 down to 8.05 across 21 seasons, delta -6.28, D1. kamara: 9.46 down to 4.03 across 9 seasons, delta -5.43, D1. Kamara's decline is the shallower of the two by this measure.
